text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bandits shoot down an army helicopter with rocket fire, killing the Samburu district commissioner and two army officers.
- The ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party nullifies the results of a local election of a KANU candidate for a parliamentary by-election, saying scores of people were barred from voting.
- President Daniel arap Moi says the government will revive an irrigation settlement scheme in Tana River district.
- President Moi criticises Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila and accuses him of destroying his country under the guise of democracy.
- Remand prisoners at Nairobi law courts protest an order barring them from receiving food from relatives and friends during court appearances.
- Fourteen people die during the Christmas period.
- The ruling Kenya African National Union party holds elections in Mombasa.
- The high court is told a Rwandan evangelist declared a prohibited immigrant has been released and gone to Uganda. ($1=55 Kenyan shillings)
